channel_name: Real Vision · Raoul Pal - The journey man
video_title: The AI Bubble Isn’t Bursting — But the Trade Is Changing | Raoul Pal The Journey Man
gist: Despite the Raoul Pal title, this is a quarterly conversation between RV Pro's Andreas and The Exponentialist's David (Raoul only introduces it). They argue AI is not a bubble — GPU rents up 40-50% since January, compute capacity-constrained, Taiwan/Korea exports at records — but the trade is shifting as CoreWeave credit stress and token-price deflation emerge, with hyperscaler earnings as the trigger, power as the next bottleneck, and model commoditization threatening OpenAI/Anthropic.

themes.theme: AI build-out: funding stress, not a bubble

insights.claim: David argues the market-legible AI build-out story is entering a new stage where not everything AI-related rises together, with stressed financials at neoclouds like CoreWeave the trigger.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Indiscriminate AI-hardware beta trades are giving way to selective positioning.

insights.claim: CoreWeave's bonds fell to distressed levels and its stock dropped 15% in about a day last week amid worries over debt-funded data center build-outs.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Neocloud credit is the weakest link in the AI capex chain.
insights.quote: It fell 15% in like a day.

insights.claim: About a trillion dollars came off memory makers during the week of recording, and a leaked Anthropic prospectus showed an $81 billion loss, much of it non-cash.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Sentiment around AI hardware is fragile and headline-driven.

insights.claim: The OpenAI revenue scare (from ~$70B talk to $50B) was mainly an accounting presentation matter, yet the market overreacted and it helped spark the sell-off.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: The market is twitchy and overreacts to small AI news.

insights.claim: Both hosts reject the bubble narrative, citing Howard Marks that if everyone is asking whether it's a bubble, it isn't, since bubbles require disregard of risk; Andreas adds 'we have a bubble in people calling it bubbles'.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Widespread bubble fear argues against an imminent top.
insights.quote: we have a bubble in people calling it bubbles

insights.claim: Andreas says the funding stress is more fundamental than prior AI scares like DeepSeek because 'the bond market is basically always right', and the Mag 7 and neoclouds must give bond markets a compelling capex rationale.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Credit spreads on AI borrowers are the key sentiment gauge.
insights.quote: you cannot argue with the bond market. The bond market is basically always right.

insights.claim: Meta raised its capex range rather than cutting it, and Andreas expects Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft to stay upbeat on building more in their upcoming reports.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler capex guidance should stay strong, supporting AI suppliers.
insights.quote: They up the range for capex.

insights.claim: Andreas' risk scenario: if hyperscaler earnings disappoint, stress could spread from neoclouds to hyperscalers and trigger a major correction — 'run for the hills' — especially if rates rise after a hotter inflation print.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler earnings are the binary event for AI stocks.
insights.quote: if they fail to deliver on expectations, then run for the hills

insights.claim: Taiwan and Korea exports, a decades-old leading indicator of 12-month-forward US earnings, are at record growth, suggesting the earnings peak is still far off.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Leading indicators point to continued earnings growth in tech.

insights.claim: SpaceX delivered a tremendous earnings report the day before recording, per Andreas.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: AI/space-adjacent earnings remain strong.

insights.claim: Unlike the dot-com era, when bandwidth prices fell 90% in 2000-2003 and fiber utilization was very low, current compute is highly utilized and capacity-constrained.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: The fiber-glut analogy for AI capex is flawed.

insights.claim: Anthropic's IPO prospectus says it struggles to get capacity and has been refused by several Mag 7 suppliers, which Andreas says explains OpenAI's market-share gains.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Compute access is a competitive determinant among AI labs.

insights.claim: GPU rental prices for both B200 Blackwell and older H100 chips are still rising, up about 40-50% since January 1, the opposite of what oversupply would produce.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Rising GPU rents contradict the overbuild thesis and support neocloud revenues.
insights.quote: we're up 40-50% in rental prices on GPUs just since first of Jan

insights.claim: Andreas says every investment bank DCF he reviewed assumes falling GPU rental prices, so rising rents imply the market is too worried about financing relative to asset values.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Consensus models may underestimate AI infrastructure cash flows.
insights.quote: I've not found one investment banks not assuming falling GPU rental prices over time

insights.claim: Neocloud borrowing rates are up roughly 40-50% this year but so are GPU rents, and since build-outs aren't fully debt-funded, Andreas argues neoclouds are net better off than on January 1; the nasty scenario would be falling GPU prices plus rising rates.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Watch for GPU price declines as the real danger signal for neocloud credit.

insights.claim: Anthropic revenue rose from about $1.1 billion in H1 2025 to roughly $16 billion in H1 2026 while compute costs rose 4-5x (he called the revenue growth about 50x, though the stated figures imply roughly 15x), suggesting it is outpacing compute costs.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Lab unit economics are improving despite falling token prices.

insights.claim: Andreas' main worry as an AI hardware investor is falling average token prices: if token pricing converges toward zero, it's unclear how chips get paid for.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Token price deflation is the long-run risk to AI hardware returns.
insights.quote: if the token pricing converges to what, zero? How on earth are we going to pay for all of the chips?

insights.claim: David argues AI agents using AI will eventually be the vast majority of compute use, alongside autonomous vehicles and robots, so fears of overbuilding are misplaced.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Long-run compute demand likely exceeds current build plans.

themes.theme: Model commoditization and the lab business model

insights.claim: David argues 'good enough' intelligence used by 99% of users is being commoditized, the deepest structural challenge for OpenAI and Anthropic, forcing them to compete on UX, context and 'AI magic'.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Value may accrue to distribution owners rather than model makers.

insights.claim: More US enterprises are shifting spending to DeepSeek because it is cheaper and good enough, making it a genuine competitive threat to OpenAI and Anthropic.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Open/cheap Chinese models pressure frontier lab pricing.

insights.claim: Momentum has shifted from Anthropic (dominant around Christmas with Opus 4.6) to OpenAI after its Astra release; on benchmarks Astra is better at computer use and Claude Fable at long-chain reasoning and coding, a toss-up.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Lab leadership is rotating quickly; no durable model moat.

insights.claim: David warns the ultimate AI value may go to distribution giants like Meta (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram plus its Muse agent) and Google rather than OpenAI and Anthropic.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Meta and Alphabet may be better AI monetization plays than standalone labs.

insights.claim: Andreas speculates that Amodei, Altman and Musk all favor AI regulation because it would create a soft floor under token prices against open-source competitors.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Regulation could protect incumbent lab pricing power.

insights.claim: David reads Dario Amodei's 'Pace the Frontier' essay, warning of AI agent swarms within 6-12 months, as partly a pitch for regulation that bakes in incumbents' lead, though he agrees agent-swarm risks are real.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Lab safety messaging is linked to IPO and regulatory positioning.

insights.claim: Andreas says connectors (e.g. Danish bookkeeping systems opening to Claude) materially increased his token usage and create stickiness that DeepSeek lacks.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Integrations drive both token growth and lock-in for leading labs.

insights.claim: Andreas would lean against buying either the OpenAI or Anthropic IPO, but prefers OpenAI because it is better positioned on compute capacity while Claude is substantially slower due to inference constraints.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: OpenAI's compute commitments are seen as an edge over Anthropic.

insights.claim: OpenAI's hardware device with Jony Ive has still not appeared, despite being central to its lock-in strategy.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: OpenAI's consumer hardware push remains unproven.

insights.claim: DeepSeek was excluded from US civilian government systems, which David sees as the start of the US and China building rival sovereign AI stacks.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Expect more bans on cross-border AI software and hardware.

insights.claim: China is the majority player in optical transceivers, which the US administration is reportedly considering banning, so US fiber optics firms would benefit most from an import blockade.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: US fiber-optics/transceiver makers are the main beneficiaries of decoupling.

insights.claim: China has essentially no footprint in high-bandwidth memory, a little under 10% of DRAM (CXMT) and a little under 20% of NAND (YMTC).
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Memory is less exposed to US-China decoupling than optics.

insights.claim: China is restricting exports of some of its own technologies, including frontier model weights.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Two separate AI supply chains are forming.

insights.claim: Andreas sees the current bottleneck as memory/GPUs, the next as power because much data center capacity is not online for lack of power, and is positioning for power.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Power infrastructure is the next AI bottleneck trade.
insights.quote: I'm focusing on power as the next bottleneck

insights.claim: Andreas expects the deployment phase — robotics, physical AI and inference-optimized chips — to perform well into 2027-2028, but has kept his robotics sleeve small for now.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Rotate gradually toward AI users and inference over 2027-2028.

insights.claim: David suggests rotating toward users of intelligence like pharma and robotics as the next stage of the AI market story.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: AI adopters may outperform AI builders in the next phase.

insights.claim: David says enterprise AI adoption is very early; like electrification, general-purpose technologies take years to diffuse into workplaces, and even Sam Altman concedes earlier job-loss forecasts aren't playing out.
insights.speaker: David (The Exponentialist)
insights.so_what: Productivity gains from AI will lag but be large.

insights.claim: The key things to watch are hyperscaler revenue versus debt, rate expectations, and a possible Iran deal that would ease energy and inflation pressures.
insights.speaker: Andreas (RV Pro)
insights.so_what: Iran, rates and hyperscaler earnings are the main macro swing factors for AI stocks.
insights.quote: A deal with Iran would calm down things a lot.
